messages:
customer-acme: Hey team — after migrating our app to use Redwood via AWS PrivateLink we see intermittent 403s and some TLS errors from our prod pods. This started right after cutover. Anyone seen something like this?

support-bot: New support thread created: #SUP-4821 — assigning emily-support.

emily-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a short repro (curl output + dig) and say whether the endpoint is cross-account or same AWS account? Also which domain you're calling (custom domain or api.redwood.com)? :eyes:

customer-acme: Quick repro below (from one of our app hosts, EKS node in us-east-1):

```bash
$ dig +short api.redwood-company.com
10.0.12.45
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-company.com/ -o /dev/null
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood-company.com/
*   Trying 10.0.12.45...
* Connected to 10.0.12.45 (10.0.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* SSL: certificate subject name 'CN=svc.internal.redwood' does not match target host name 'api.redwood-company.com'
* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches
* Closing connection 0
* SSL certificate problem: (null)
* Couldn't connect to server
```

customer-acme: Intermittently the same hostname resolves to our NATed public IP (we saw this only on a few pods) and then we get 403s from Redwood (looks like traffic egressed to public).

michael-infra: Two quick suspects: DNS split-horizon / PHZ association and SNI/host header mismatch. Also check the endpoint security group and source/dest behavior with TGW/hairpinning if you route via a central NAT.

emily-support: Can you confirm: 1) Did you enable Private DNS on the interface VPC endpoint? 2) Is this an endpoint for a Redwood-managed service (cross-account endpoint service) or a simple interface endpoint to our account? 3) Are you using a customer CNAME that points to the public API name?

customer-acme: Answers: 1) We thought we had PrivateDNS enabled when creating the endpoint. 2) It's cross-account (our account -> redwood-infra account). 3) We CNAME our custom domain (api.redwood-company.com) to the public redwood host.

ben-oncall: If you CNAME a custom domain to the public host and then rely on the VPC endpoint private DNS, you must ensure the private hosted zone for the service is associated with your VPC and the endpoint was created with PrivateDnsEnabled=true. Otherwise clients will sometimes resolve the public IP. Also some Java/Go HTTP clients aggressively cache DNS.

emily-support: Two quick troubleshooting commands to run on a pod (please paste results):

```bash
# show VPC endpoint from host (if you have awscli credentials)
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=<your-vpc-id>" --query "VpcEndpoints[?ServiceName=='com.amazonaws.vpce.<region>.vpce-svc-...']"

# force TLS/SNI to test certificate with curl. replace <private-ip> below with the ENI IP you got from dig.
curl -v --resolve api.redwood-company.com:443:10.0.12.45 https://api.redwood-company.com/ 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
```

customer-acme: Ran these, snippets attached:

```json
# aws results (trimmed)
{ "VpcEndpoints": [ { "VpcEndpointId": "vpce-0abc1234", "ServiceName": "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-0fedcba9", "PrivateDnsEnabled": true, "State": "available" } ] }
```

```bash
# curl with --resolve output
* Connected to api.redwood-company.com (10.0.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake shows server certificate for CN=svc.internal.redwood, SANs: svc.internal.redwood, vpce-0abc1234.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com
* SSL: certificate subject name 'CN=svc.internal.redwood' does not match 'api.redwood-company.com'
```

customer-acme: We also caught a failing pod where dig returned 52.14.99.20 (public) for the same hostname right before a 403. Not sure why DNS returned public sometimes.

michael-infra: That nails it: split-horizon/caching + SNI mismatch. For PrivateLink interface endpoints, the service owner usually provides a VPCE-specific DNS name (the vpce-*.region.vpce.amazonaws.com SAN above). If your custom domain points to the public hostname and you rely on Private DNS, you must ensure the service's private hosted zone maps api.redwood-company.com to the interface endpoint ENI IP. When cross-account, the service owner (Redwood) must have set up a Private Hosted Zone and allowed the association.

michael-infra: Short list of root causes we've seen:
- Private DNS wasn't associated with your VPC (so resolution falls back to public)
- Client DNS caches old public answers (app-level caching, node resolver cache)
- TLS certificate presented by endpoint does not include your custom domain (SNI mismatch) because the endpoint is terminating TLS with svc.internal certificate
- Traffic hairpin via TGW/NAT causes return path to go via public egress and hit public LB (403)

emily-support: Practical next steps / mitigations:
1) Confirm PHZ association: from your tenant side run `aws route53 get-hosted-zone` (or ask us to confirm association).
2) If PHZ association cannot be done immediately, short-term workaround: add an /etc/hosts entry on app nodes mapping api.redwood-company.com -> 10.0.12.45 (private ENI IP) to avoid public resolution.
3) For SNI mismatch, either: a) use the VPCE DNS name (vpce-...amazonaws.com) in your app SNI/Host header; or b) have Redwood add your custom domain to the service's cert SANs (requires Redwood to provision cert for that hostname or support TLS passthrough).
4) Reduce app DNS cache TTL or restart pods to clear cached records.
5) If you have TGW / central NAT, ensure routes to the ENI are local (no NAT egress) so traffic doesn't hairpin to the public LB.

emily-support: Quick curl tests you can run to validate SNI vs cert:

```bash
# Force SNI to the endpoint DNS name (should match SAN on cert)
curl -v --resolve api.redwood-company.com:443:10.0.12.45 https://api.redwood-company.com/
# Force host header to the vpce hostname so SNI uses vpce name (if your client supports separate SNI and Host header)
curl -v --header 'Host: vpce-0abc1234.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com' --resolve vpce-0abc1234.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com:443:10.0.12.45 https://vpce-0abc1234.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com/
```

customer-acme: Thanks — we confirmed private DNS was associated but it looks like our app's JVM caches the public answer for 5 minutes. Also the cert doesn't include our custom domain; it includes only internal svc names and the vpce hostname. We can either have Redwood add our custom domain (preferred) or switch to using the vpce host.

emily-support: We can do two things on our side: 1) open an internal request to add your custom domain to the service cert (need your exact domain and verification), or 2) enable TLS passthrough / preserve SNI so your original SNI is honored — both require ops changes. For immediate unblock, use the vpce host and set Host header to the public hostname if you'd like header-based routing, or add the hosts entry as a stopgap.

ben-oncall: Also check security group on vpce-ENIs: inbound 443 must allow your app subnets. If you use a central firewall/egress allowlist, ensure 10.0.12.45 (ENI) and vpce service IPs are allowed. We saw customers block the ENI IPs in Zscaler/firewall and it caused 502/403 flakiness.

customer-acme: We'll patch the JVM DNS cache TTL and try using the vpce host for a quick test. If we still want the custom domain, please start the cert/SAN request.

emily-support: Got it — we've logged an internal ticket to evaluate adding your cname to our certs. Emily to follow up with Ops for cert/SAN work and verification steps. For now please paste the output of `tcpdump -n -s 0 -w - port 443 and host 10.0.12.45` if you see another failure and we can examine handshake SNI and source IPs.

customer-acme: Will do, thanks all. Really appreciate the quick triage. :pray: 

emily-support: Thanks — marking as investigating, will update thread when Ops confirms cert/SAN plan.
